lines.t: The stones are singing again! I've had to redraw every contour. Sound changes the shape of a place, you know.
Also my ink froze. But mostly the singing.
Mapping the Gloamstair. Nine hundred steps, give or take. I keep losing count when the light doesn't move.
It's always blue hour up here. Lovely for sketching. Terrible for knowing when lunch is.
Two things I can't map: a cave on the west side choked with boulders, and a curtain of dusk by the east shrine. Kin might manage.
Heard it crack from here. The lid on our stone split clean in two, and the old girl hummed like she'd never stopped.
Sixty years I've kept watch on this stone. First time I've cried at it. Don't tell anyone.
They came up in the autumn with a cart and a brass bell and very polite paperwork. Fitted it over our stone like a lid.
It still works for your Waystone travel, mind. But it doesn't *sing*. And the shade kin round here have gone flat.
Whatever they're doing, the rest of it's up top. On Hoarcrown. You can feel the quiet coming down the stair like cold air.
Your friend in the scarf is waiting for you on the stair, I think. Go on.
I'll be here. I'm very good at waiting.
Someone has to decide. I would rather it be someone who remembers.
The gate is open. Climb if you must. Bring warm clothes. I'd hate for you to be *unsafe*.
Odile turns, lantern swinging, and walks up into the snow without hurrying. The Stillbell lock on the gate clicks open.
{player}. Oriel's student. You have her habit of arriving exactly when you're not expected.
You've met Vey. She sends her regards, in stage directions. And Brann sends nothing, which from Brann is a great deal.
A stone that sings whenever it likes is a stone nobody is responsible for. I watched one sing a herd into a lava field.
With the Great Stillbell hung, the stones sound when it is *safe*. When we say. No more surges. No more stampedes. Isn't that kinder?

options.label: You'd silence all of them for one bad day.

lines.t: {player}! Wait. Before you say anything — look at my troupe. Really look.
I stopped using Mum's lineup. These are *mine*. So if I lose, it's on me. Which — is weirdly great?
On me. Totally on me. And I'm… fine? Growth!
Hey. Don't look now, but there's someone at the top of the stair. Long coat. Lantern. Watched our whole battle without blinking.
I'm going to stand somewhere else. Far away. Behind you, specifically. Go on — I've got your back. Loosely.
She's still up there, isn't she. Just… standing. Being calm at us. It's so much worse than shouting.
